statement: A magma of order n >= 1 satisfying x = y(y(x(xy))) exists if and only if n = 0 or 1 (mod 4). Necessity: x # y = x(xy) is a semi-symmetric quasigroup (law 14) whose left translations are squares L_x^2, hence even, while every finite semi-symmetric quasigroup of order n has prod_y sign(L_y) = (-1)^(n(n-1)/2), because (x, y) -> (y, x # y) has order 3. Sufficiency: on A = Z_n (n odd) or Z_2 x Z_2 x Z_{n/4} (4 | n), x # y = -x - y has involutive translations with an even number of 2-cycles; their square roots sigma_x give the model x * y = sigma_x(y).
title: The spectrum of ETP law 501, x = y(y(x(xy))), is exactly {n : n = 0, 1 (mod 4)}
